text: When the chapter is set beside the earlier promise, their difference is narrowed; for Isaac is still the child of the covenant, and the one through whom the nations are to be blessed, while that very promise is made the matter of the test in Genesis 22. The scene turns upon the single Hebrew word hineni, "here I am," which Abraham speaks three times, to God, to Isaac, and to the angel. At each utterance the word bears another sense; at each return it costs Abraham more. Presence to God and to others is here inseparable from loss, when Abraham says, "here I am,"
